learning_objective: 🎯 Journey to the center of the Earth! Since we can't dig that deep, learn how scientists use earthquake waves to figure out what's hidden miles beneath our feet.

main_concepts.simple_explanation: We can't travel to the Earth's core. We use Direct sources (mining, drilling, volcanic eruptions) and Indirect sources (gravity, magnetic fields, and most importantly, seismic earthquake waves) to understand the interior.

Earthquakes release energy waves. 'P-waves' (Primary) are fast and travel through solids, liquids, and gases. 'S-waves' (Secondary) are slower and ONLY travel through solid materials. Their paths tell us what the Earth is made of.

Earth is like an onion. The outer layer is the solid Crust. Below is the Mantle (which contains the semi-liquid asthenosphere where magma comes from). The innermost part is the Core (outer core is liquid iron, inner core is solid).
Places where gases, ashes, and molten rock material (magma) escape to the ground. Types include Shield volcanoes (mostly lava, gentle slopes) and Composite volcanoes (explosive, steep mountains).

fun_activity.title: 🥚 The Hard-Boiled Earth
fun_activity.instructions: Cut a hard-boiled egg in half. The thin shell is the Earth's Crust. The thick white part is the Mantle. The yellow yolk in the center is the Core. This is the perfect visual model for the structure of our planet!

exam_tips: 📌 The 'Shadow Zone' is a highly tested concept. S-waves have a shadow zone beyond 105°, proving that the outer core is liquid because S-waves cannot travel through liquids.
📌 Distinguish between Focus (Hypocenter) where the earthquake actually originates inside the earth, and the Epicenter, which is the point directly above it on the surface.
📌 The Lithosphere consists of the Crust AND the uppermost solid part of the Mantle.
quick_recap: ⭐ Seismic waves are the most important indirect source of information about the Earth's interior.
⭐ P-waves travel through all mediums, while S-waves travel only through solids.
⭐ The Asthenosphere is the main source of magma that finds its way to the surface during volcanic eruptions.
